key_insight: The explog formulation improves acoustic-term accuracy in weakly-compressible SPH while running faster than the naive formulation on GPU and only marginally slower on CPU.
engineering_relevance: More accurate acoustic calculations support energy conservation and reliable solid and open boundary behavior in GPU-based SPH simulations.
method: Reformulate the equation of state, its inverse, and local sound speed using explog.
Rewrite pressure evaluation for dummy-model solid boundary particles.
Assess numerical accuracy and computational performance across devices and test cases.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a maximum error of 2 ULP for arguments below 0.125, higher errors for fewer than 1% of arguments above that threshold, and pressure-profile deviations below 2% even over rough terrain.
watch_item: Accuracy is not uniformly bounded at 2 ULP above the reported threshold, and CPU evaluation incurs a small performance penalty.
paper_title: Computational performance versus numerical accuracy in the acoustic terms of weakly-compressible SPH
